newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIAN CRIME UP 9.2 PCT IN H1 1997-MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIAN CRIME UP 9.2 PCT IN H1 1997-MINISTER.

text.p: Crime in Hungary rose almost 10 percent in the first half of this year and domestic measures were no longer effective against international organised crime, Hungary's Minister of Interior said on Wednesday.
"There is no international body to deal with it, so Hungary does its best by concluding bilateral agreements," Gabor Kuncze told a news conference.
He added that the number of crimes in Hungary continued to rise in the first half of 1997 at a 9.2 percent rate, but the number of murders and car thefts has decreased.

He added that while the total number of crimes rose to 234,444 cases in the first half of the year, up 9.2 percent on the first half of last year, murders declined to 125 from 135 and car thefts fell to 6,232 from 6,720.
Last month a high-ranking police official said Hungary has become a European crossroads for organised crime and the international police response to combat the upsurge has been inadequate.

Apart from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), organised crime was also imported into Hungary from South America, Turkey, Italy, Nigeria and Kosovo, in Serbia, police officials said earlier.
Hungary has already concluded 15 bilateral agreements on fighting organised crime and a number of others were being negotiated, Kuncze said.
Economic crime rose in absolute numbers, but almost halved in forint terms to 6.3 billion forints from 11.2 billion, a ministry report showed.
However, the damage recovery rate also more than halved to 20.2 percent from last year's 47.9 percent, the report said.
